refnamediv.refpurpose: Set blocking/non-blocking mode on a stream

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
boolstream_set_blocking resourcestream boolenable
Sets blocking or non-blocking mode on a stream.
This function works for any stream that supports non-blocking mode (currently, regular files, socket streams, pipes such as those of popen and proc_open, STDIN, FIFOs, and user-space stream wrappers).

&reftitle.parameters;
stream
The stream.
enable
If enable is &false;, the given stream will be switched to non-blocking mode, and if &true;, it will be switched to blocking mode. This affects calls like fgets and fread that read from the stream. In non-blocking mode an fgets call will always return right away while in blocking mode it will wait for data to become available on the stream.
When no data is available in non-blocking mode, fread returns an empty string, fgets returns &false; and feof stays &false;. Data that is already in the read buffer is still returned first. The blocked and unread_bytes entries of stream_get_meta_data show the current state.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
&return.success; &true; is also returned for streams that have no blocking mode, such as php://memory, php://temp, php://output, php://input, data:// streams and directory handles: the call then has no effect. &false; is returned if the mode cannot be changed on the descriptor, or if the streamWrapper::stream_set_option method of a user-space wrapper returns a falsy value or is missing.

&reftitle.notes;
On Windows, this has no affect on local files. Non-blocking IO for local files is not supported on Windows.
The mode belongs to the file description, which is shared with the process that started PHP. After stream_set_blocking(STDIN, false), standard input stays non-blocking when the script ends, and a program reading from it afterwards can fail with "Resource temporarily unavailable".
A Socket object is not accepted: use socket_set_block or socket_set_nonblock instead.
